summary: Federated cross-cloud access provisioning failing for periodic security-audit run
description:
Issue summary: The periodic security-audit job that provisions short-lived cross-cloud access (GCP workload identity -> AWS assume-role) fails during automated provisioning. The failure started after the org-wide tag policy rollout on 2026-03-09 and prevents the audit runner from accessing encrypted S3 artifacts and KMS-protected keys in the AWS audit account.

Impact: Security team cannot run scheduled audit batches for customer-scoped logs for two internal customers. Blocking next weekly compliance report. No direct customer-facing outage, but a compliance and attestation risk.

Environment: Provisioner runs from staging-control-plane (k8s) in us-west; target resources in aws-audit-prod (us-east-1) and gcp-logs-prod (us-central1).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger provisioner via /run-audit endpoint in staging-control-plane pod audit-provisioner-5f6d
2) Provisioner requests a GCP service account token and calls internal 'confed-provision' service to create a federated identity binding
3) confed-provision attempts to create IAM Role on aws-audit-prod account via assume-role chain but receives AccessDenied due to missing required org:tag on the role creation request
4) Provisioner falls back to queued retry; retries produce same AccessDenied with different request IDs
logs: Provisioner error: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/infra-bot/session is not authorized to perform: iam:CreateRole on resource: arn:aws:iam::777888999000:role/audit-provision-role because of Organization policy 'require-org-tag' (RequestID: 9b8f2c4a)
KMS access attempt: AccessDeniedException when decrypting audit-shared-key: insufficient kms:Decrypt permissions for principal via assumed role
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: org-trust tags enforced by new org policy block role creation unless request includes 'org:project' tag from a whitelisted tag source. Provisioner does not currently propagate the required tagging metadata when creating the cross-account role. Observed that infra-bot has broad assume-role permissions but the CreateRole call is intercepted by org policy guardrails at the AWS control plane. Verified with AWS org admin that policy was pushed on 2026-03-09.

Checked IAM: infra-bot principal can assume existing audit-provision-role but cannot create new roles without the required tags. Confed-provision's code path tries to create ephemeral roles for each audit tenant to ensure isolation. Recent PR to add tagging metadata to role creation was merged but the image deployed to staging-control-plane is older (image tag v1.9.3 vs v1.10.0 contains fix).
temporary_workaround: Manually provision a templated role with the required org:project tag in the aws-audit-prod account for the two impacted tenants and add it to the provisioner allowlist. This restores audit run access for the immediate batch. Manual steps documented in confluence page linked above.
next_steps: 1) Roll forward confed-provision to image v1.10.0 in staging-control-plane and run end-to-end repro. 2) Add automated unit/integration test to ensure required org tags are present on CreateRole API calls. 3) Request AWS Org admin to add a scoped exception for infra-bot for one maintenance window while we roll the fix to prod. 4) Backfill a migration script to add required tags to previously created ephemeral roles. 5) Postmortem and adjust deployment pipeline to include a gating test for org-policy compatibility.
